Effective May 1, 2026, the California Department of Public Health implemented a quarantine on all species of sport-harvested mussels taken for human consumption along the entire California coast. The quarantine area extends from the Oregon border south to the Mexican border, including all bays, inlets, and harbors. 

CLICK HERE FOR MORE INFORMATION

This quarantine is in addition to all advisories published on this map.

The California Department of Public Health (CDPH) has lifted the shellfish safety notifications related to sport-harvested clams, scallops, and oysters from {County_Name}. The statewide mussel quarantine is still in effect.

Safety notifications are issued due to dangerous levels of naturally occurring PSP and/or Domoic Acid toxins. Recent testing shows the biotoxins have decreased to safe or undetectable levels in {County_Name} county (Press Release). Safety notifications are still in effect for other California counties.

Please follow all Shellfish Safety Notifications or call CDPH's Shellfish Information Line at (800) 553-4133.

popupElements.text:
SHELLFISH SAFETY NOTIFICATION WILL REMAIN IN PLACE FOR ALL NORTHERN CHANNEL ISLANDS

This advisory remains in place because additional samples are required to lift the advisory. 

The California Department of Public Health (CDPH) is advising the public not to consume sport-harvested mussels, clams, scallops, or oysters from the Northern Channel Islands (Anacapa, Santa Cruz, Santa Rosa, and San Miguel).


 

Dangerous levels of domoic acid have been detected in mussels from the Northern Channel Islands. The naturally occurring domoic acid toxin can cause illness or death in humans. Cooking does not destroy the toxin.

Domoic acid poisoning can occur within 30 minutes to 24 hours after eating toxic seafood. In mild cases, symptoms may include vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal cramps, headache, and dizziness. These symptoms disappear within several days. In severe cases, the victim may experience trouble breathing, confusion, disorientation, cardiovascular instability, seizures, excessive bronchial secretions, permanent loss of short-term memory, coma, or death.

 

This warning does not apply to commercially sold clams, mussels, scallops, or oysters from approved sources. State law permits only state-certified commercial shellfish harvesters or dealers to sell these products. Shellfish sold by certified harvesters and dealers are subject to frequent mandatory testing to monitor for toxins.

Please follow all Shellfish Safety Notifications or call CDPH's Shellfish Information Line at (800) 553-4133. You can also download a list of recent CDPH biotoxin testing results. 

Press Release

popupElements.text:
The California Department of Public Health is advising consumers not to eat sport-harvested razor clams from Del Norte or Humboldt counties.


Dangerous levels of domoic acid, also referred to as Amnesic Shellfish Poisoning, have been detected in razor clams from these counties (Results). This warning only applies to razor clams as they are known to concentrate and retain domoic acid toxin in their meat and tissues at higher levels and for much longer than other species of bivalve shellfish. The naturally occurring domoic acid toxin can cause illness or death in humans. Cooking does not destroy the toxin.
 

Please follow all Shellfish Safety Notifications or call CDPH's Shellfish Information Line at (800) 553-4133.

 

Updated July 29, 2026

popupElements.text:
SHELLFISH SAFETY NOTIFICATION issued for {COUNTY_NAME}

The California Department of Public Health (CDPH) is advising the public not to consume sport-harvested mussels, clams (including razor clams), scallops, or oysters from {County_Name}.

Dangerous levels of paralytic shellfish poisoning (PSP) toxins have been detected in mussels from {County_Name}. The naturally occurring PSP toxins can cause illness or death in humans. Cooking does not destroy the toxin.

PSP toxins affect the nervous system, producing a tingling around the mouth and fingertips within a few minutes to a few hours after eating toxic shellfish. These symptoms are typically followed by loss of balance, lack of muscular coordination, slurred speech, and difficulty swallowing. In severe poisonings, complete muscular paralysis and death from asphyxiation can occur.

This warning does not apply to commercially sold clams, mussels, scallops, or oysters from approved sources. State law permits only state-certified commercial shellfish harvesters or dealers to sell these products. Shellfish sold by certified harvesters and dealers are subject to frequent mandatory testing to monitor for toxins.

Please follow all Shellfish Safety Notifications or call CDPH's Shellfish Information Line at (800) 553-4133.
